title: Raman spectroscopy of van der Waals topological magnet GdGaI
authors: Nan Jiang, Yijin Zhang, Yujie Xia, Tomo Higashihara, Ryutaro Okuma, Jun-ichi Yamaura, Yoshinori Okada, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Tiantian Zhang, Tomoki Machida, Yasuhiro Niimi
abstract: We report polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy of a van der Waals compound GdGaI that is a candidate for excitonic insulators. By combining the symmetry analysis with density functional theory calculations, we identify six Raman-active phonons. The spectra exhibit only the expected anharmonic hardening down to 4 K: no additional peaks, no soft modes, and no signatures of zone folding are observed. This result indicates that any lattice distortion is below our experimental sensitivity, supporting an electronically driven origin for the band reconstruction reported by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy rather than an electron-phonon-driven mechanism. Moreover, we observe a pronounced circular dichroism of the $A_{1g}$ modes under an out-of-plane magnetic field. Based on symmetry considerations, we attribute this dichroic response to chiral $A_{1g}$ phonons with opposite angular momenta generated by spin-phonon coupling in the time-reversal-broken state. The temperature evolution of the degree of circular polarization further suggests that circularly polarized Raman spectroscopy detects the emergence of short-range antiferromagnetic correlations. Our results highlight GdGaI as a promising platform in which excitonic order, magnetism, and circularly polarized phonons can be intertwined, and demonstrate that circular-polarization Raman provides a sensitive probe of spin-phonon coupling in excitonic systems.
summary: This paper uses polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy on GdGaI to investigate the nature of its insulating state. By showing no evidence of lattice distortion characteristic of CDW systems, they argue for an electronic origin for band reconstruction. Furthermore, observing magnetic field-dependent circular dichroism confirms spin-phonon coupling, positioning GdGaI as a model system where excitonic order and magnetism interact via phonons.
main_problem: To distinguish between excitonic insulator (EI) transitions and conventional charge-density-wave (CDW) systems, both involving band reconstruction in the van der Waals magnet GdGaI.
main_result: The absence of soft modes or zone folding supports an electronically driven origin for band reconstruction, while circular dichroism reveals spin-phonon coupling linked to short-range antiferromagnetic correlations.
method: Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy combined with symmetry analysis and DFT calculations were used to probe lattice vibrations under varying magnetic fields and temperatures.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the van der Waals topological magnet GdGaI, investigating its interplay between excitonic order, magnetism, and phonon dynamics. The theoretical framework involves analyzing Raman tensor components sensitive to time-reversal symmetry breaking.
key_observables: Raman-active phonons ($A_{1g}, E_g$), degree of circular dichroism ($	ext{RR}/	ext{LL}$ contrast), temperature evolution of polarization, and phonon frequency shifts relative to thermal expansion models.
important_parameters: Temperature range (down to 4 K) and out-of-plane magnetic field strength ($\pm 9$ T).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the absence of spectral anomalies implies lattice distortions are below experimental sensitivity, ruling out a CDW mechanism.
figures_summary: Figures show polarized Raman spectra at various temperatures and magnetic fields, demonstrating both the lack of expected softening/folding (Fig. 3) and the clear field-dependent circular dichroism in $A_{1g}$ modes (Fig. 5).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the phonon spectrum via DFT and initial measurements; it then uses temperature dependence to rule out CDW mechanisms, followed by magnetic field studies to reveal spin-phonon coupling signatures.
why_interesting: The work provides a direct experimental link between lattice vibrations (phonons) and emergent electronic/magnetic orders (excitonic insulators, antiferromagnetism), which is crucial for understanding strongly correlated materials where electron-lattice interactions are key.
